136	### 2. `restore_after`: the DAG, its order, its limits
137	
138	**2.1 Meaning.** `BlockDescriptor.restore_after` (ADR-0003 § 2) lists the blocks that must be **restored and post-restored before this one, and initialised (`default_state`, `init_world`) before this one**. One relation orders all four callables. A block may list a non-persisted block; a `WORLD` block listing a `PROFILE` block is legal and the edge is simply not visited by an in-session pass.
139	
140	**2.2 Compilation at the freeze.** In the registry validation pass (ADR-0003 § 8, after the hook schedule) the kernel builds the `RestorePlan`:
141	
142	1. Resolve every id to the block's **registration index**; an unregistered id is `UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY` (code 10, existing). A duplicate entry in one list is dropped with a boot warning `RESTORE_AFTER_DUPLICATE` (warnings must be empty at the end of every CI run, as for hooks).
143	2. Run Kahn's algorithm over registration indices. **The ready list is ordered by registration index and the smallest ready index is always taken**, exactly the rule of the hook sort (ADR-0003 § 8), so there is one algorithm and a total order that is a pure function of registration data. Dictionary iteration never decides anything.
144	3. If unprocessed blocks remain with no ready block (this includes a block listing itself), boot fails with `RESTORE_CYCLE` (**new code**) naming the remaining blocks in registration order.
145	4. Record `order` (block indices in restore order) and `rank` (position per index), and derive three views: `world_order` (persisted `WORLD` blocks), `post_order` (`WORLD` persisted plus non-persisted blocks) and `bind_order` (blocks with a `binding_source`, ascending `String(block_id)`, § 6). The plan is immutable after the freeze and printable (`describe()`), like the hook schedule.
146	
147	Registering more than `MAX_BLOCKS` blocks fails boot with `BLOCK_LIMIT` (**new code**) at the first excess registration (TR-cmd-035). The cost of the sort at `MAX_BLOCKS` is a one-time O(n²) over at most that many entries.
148	
149	**2.3 The tie-break is load-bearing.** Probe P2 shows several valid orders of the same MVP graph under different tie-breaks. Any block that reads a non-predecessor's derived state would work under one and fail under another. That is the point of making the order a total function of registration data and of testing against other linear extensions (§ 8): the rule "a block depends only on what it declares" is enforced by the permutation test, not by trust.
150	
151	**2.4 The MVP order** (computed 2026-10-29 by a throwaway script applying § 2.2 to the architecture's registration order, Layout, Graph, Body, Controller, Emitter, Suit, Interaction, Assembly, Web, Attention, Horror, Sanity; the kernel prints the authoritative order at the freeze and this table is illustrative):
152	
153	| Pos | Block | `restore_after` (from the owner GDD or ADR) | Source |
154	|---|---|---|---|
155	| 0 | `kernel.clock` | (kernel-internal, installed at R2, not in the DAG) | ADR-0003 § 10 |
156	| 1 | `layout.state` | `[]` (the root) | ADR-0013 § 1 |
157	| 2 | `graph.state` | `[layout.state]` | ADR-0011 § 1 |
158	| 3 | `body.state` | `[layout.state]` | BDY-5 |
159	| 4 | `suit.state` | `[]` | SE-34 |
160	| 5 | `controller.state` | `[body.state, suit.state]` | ADR-0019 § 2.1 |
161	| 6 | `emitter.state` | `[layout.state, graph.state, body.state, controller.state]` | EM-1 |
162	| 7 | `interaction.state` | `[layout.state, controller.state, graph.state, body.state, emitter.state]` | IA-36 |
163	| 8 | `assembly.state` | `[layout.state, graph.state, interaction.state, body.state]` | MSA-4 |
164	| 9 | `web.state` | `[layout.state, graph.state, body.state]` | WM-2 |
165	| 10 | `attention.state` | `[graph.state, emitter.state]` | AT registration |
166	| 11 | `horror.state` | `[layout.state, graph.state, emitter.state, attention.state]` | HE-3 |
167	| 12 | `sanity.state` | `[]` | SN-1 |
168	| 13 | `sanity.ledger` | `[sanity.state, graph.state, layout.state, horror.state]` | SN-1 |
169	| 14 | `sanity.perception` | non-persisted; **assumed** `[sanity.state, sanity.ledger]` (the GDD gives none; Open Question 1) | SN-1 |
170	
171	That is 13 persisted blocks plus the clock (the 14 of SL-19) and one derived block. The DAG is acyclic: Layout is the only root of the layout chain, Suit and Sanity have no outgoing edge to the Controller or each other, and the Controller's edges go only to Body and Suit (verified by reading the owner GDDs; neither Body nor Suit declares an edge back, ADR-0019's cross-ADR assumption).
172	
173	### 3. The block contract at restore: two phases, three read tiers
174	
175	**3.1 Two phases per block, restated once (ADR-0006 § 2.2 is the rule; this ADR adds the pass-level consequences).** `restore(data, stored_version, ctx)` decodes and validates into scratch (phase 1, cold path, allocation allowed, **no write to the live block**), then, on success only, copies the contents into the existing block object and rebuilds the block's *static* derived members (phase 2). A failure is `ctx.fault(<OWNER>_RESTORE_*, detail)` with the live block untouched. The scratch object must contain no reference cycle (probe P3: a cycle leaks and `OBJECT_COUNT` shows it).
176	
177	**3.2 What `restore` may read.** Its own `data`, and **Tier S** reads of blocks in its transitive `restore_after` closure (§ 3.4). It writes only its own block. It never calls another owner's mutator, never reads `kernel.clock` `T` for a decision (the clock is installed at R2 and is read-only), and never reads a non-predecessor.
178	
179	**3.3 Defaults go through `restore`.** `default_state(ctx)` of a persisted block ends with `ctx.put(payload)` where `payload` has the shape and `schema_version` of a snapshot; the kernel applies it by calling **that block's own `restore`** with `stored_version = schema_version`. One copy path means the default is validated on every new game and every absent-block restore, a `default_state` that its own `restore` rejects fails the first test that builds a world, and the block's "registered-but-unrestored" hash (ADR-0011 § 4.6, ADR-0013 `counters` at 1) is what restore produces. If a persisted block's `default_state` returns without `put`, the pass faults with `DEFAULT_STATE_NO_PAYLOAD` (**new code**). For a non-persisted block `default_state` only resets derived members and `put` is not expected.
180	
181	**3.4 Read tiers across blocks.** Every read-view method of every block is documented as one of two tiers (a doc tag read by the lint of § 8 and printed by the Debug Overlay):
182	
183	- **Tier S (persisted-answerable).** Answerable from the block's persisted columns and the static derived members its `restore` rebuilt. Valid as soon as that block's `restore` returned. Layout's class 1 (`room_at`, `V`, `exposed_tiles`, `socket_plan`, `section_offset`, `body_of`, static rects; ADR-0013 § 10, TR-section-008), the Graph's `opening_into`, `seam_openings_into`, `section_counts_into`, `RoomSource` and `step_no`, Body's `seat_bindings()`, and any `ids below next_*` check are Tier S.
184	- **Tier D (derived).** Needs the block's own `post_restore`. Layout's class 2 (door-leaf rects, `clip_to_footprints`, `leaf_would_overlap`, `door_passage_into`), the Graph's served and band caches, the Emitter's static layer. Before the owner's `post_restore` ran, a Tier D read returns the template default (or neutral value) and raises the owner's `stale_*` diagnostic (Layout's `stale_leaf` is the first instance).
185	
186	The rule that makes order matter and keeps it checkable: **in `post_restore(X)` the callable may read Tier S of any block and Tier D only of blocks that precede X in the DAG's closure.** `restore` is stricter: Tier S of closure predecessors only. No hook, command or presentation read happens between the stages, so a stale read can occur only inside the pass.
187	
188	### 4. The `post_restore` contract
189	
190	**4.1 Order.** `post_restore` runs in `post_order`, which is `order` filtered; it is the same DAG as `restore`. Reasons: architecture § Data Flow 7 already states it; Emitter Open Question 26 and ADR-0019 (Controller after Suit) need it; the cost is zero because the DAG exists; and "informational only" (Layout) means no rule depends on it, which is compatible. After this ADR Layout's `version`/`leaf_version` self-heal (LY-12 d) stays as belt and braces and is no longer what makes the Emitter's cold build correct for open doors.
191	
192	**4.2 Write policy (closed).**
193	
194	| Class | May `post_restore(X)` do it? | Rule |
195	|---|---|---|
196	| Rebuild X's **derived** members (caches, lookups, version counters, seeds of last-emitted values) | Yes | Writes no persisted column and draws no RNG. |
197	| Write X's **persisted** columns | **No**, except block X is on `REBASE_BLOCKS` (§ 9) | A normalisation belongs in `snapshot()`; see § 9. |
198	| Write any **other** block | **No** | `open_for` of another block in the `RESTORE` scope is `REFUSED` and a counted `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` violation (ADR-0003 § 4). |
199	| Submit a command | **No** (impossible) | `SnapshotContext` has no `submit_system`. |
200	| Clamp, prune, repair or default a persisted value | **No** | A bad value is a fault; a well-formed but semantically dead reference restores as it is (TR-sanity-019). |
201	| Raise a fault | Yes | Only for a check of § 5; first failure wins. |
202	
203	**4.3 Reconciliation is an ordinary hook rule, not a restore step.** Anything a block would like to "fix up after a load" (the Graph's stock reconcile, Interaction's subject window, Attention's beacon, Sanity's dead-subject prune) is performed by the owner's **next hook run under a normal `HOOK` scope**, and it must be **the same rule that runs every tick**, a no-op when state is consistent, with no `just_restored` flag. Reason: kernel G4 demands the same `state_hash` at every tick from a restored run and an uninterrupted run; a reconcile that exists only on the first post-restore run would diverge from the uninterrupted run whenever it does anything, and a reconcile that does nothing in the uninterrupted run is exactly an idempotent steady-state rule. KRN-RST-11 checks each owner's reconcile this way (600 ticks, hash per tick).
204	
205	**4.4 Consequences for the cited rows.**
206	- **Layout/Graph stock reconcile (TR-itemdb-033).** The Graph keeps ADR-0011 § 7.3: a store above a lowered live `stock_cap` restores byte-identically (it is below the physical ceiling `max_stock_*`), and the clamp, the `discarded_*` credit, the `stock_clamped` count and the diagnostic naming node, old stock and cap run at the head of phase 0 of the first Graph step. `post_restore` does not clamp (§ 4.2), so the K-4 verdict is `MATCH` and no REBASED cause is owed to ADR-0006.
207	- **Catalogue tuning drift (TR-itemdb-032).** A `restore` or `post_restore` check is either **structural** (shape, range, id order, reference resolution, a physical ceiling) or it is not a restore check. A value that is a catalogue tunable (mass, `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G`, `GLOWSTICK_STACK_MAX`, `PATCH_CAP_BP`, `stock_cap`, a def's rated output) is never asserted, clamped, deleted or migrated at restore. A `def_id` that no longer resolves is a structural failure (`RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF`), and an alias renamed by ADR-0007's path resolves.
208	- **Interaction (TR-interact-016, -017, TR-boarding-005).** § 5 row V-IA and § 9: Interaction's `post_restore` may not write the Emitter or the Controller; `loose[].inst` decode is a verifier; channel and door-attempt dropping is an interim normalisation.
209	- **Body (TR-shipbody-010).** `pos_prev := pos_curr` is a derived-member rebuild; `sub` is preserved (persisted, untouched); the trapped-actor probe counts and never faults; Body never rebuilds the kernel seat binding.
210	- **Attention (TR-attention-025).** `post_restore` rebuilds caches only; the beacon is reconciled by the first `attention.step` by comparing persisted `beacon_commanded` with Emitter state (§ 4.3); no cue fires on load because cues fire on transitions and the kernel's `ALL` batch carries no transition.
211	- **Sanity (TR-sanity-019).** `post_restore` must not prune; a well-formed dead `subject_ref` restores, is projected as it is and is invalidated by the next hook run.
212	
213	### 5. Cross-block verification: where the checks live and the order they run in
214	
215	**5.1 Decision.** Verifiers are **distributed, never kernel-held**. Each is a pure, read-only function in the owning block's `restore` or `verify` file, called from that block's `post_restore` (or `restore` where the check needs only Tier S of a predecessor), at the block's position in the DAG. The kernel only runs the callables in order and turns the first fault into `FAULTED`. This keeps H1 (no domain rule in the kernel), keeps the TR rows' wording ("in `post_restore`"), and needs no new registrar surface. The central artefact is **this ADR's numbered list**, which fixes what is checked and in which block's slot; the owner ADRs fix the check bodies.
216	
217	**5.2 Verifier shape.** A verifier is `static func verify_restore(views: <Owner>VerifierViews, out: VerifyOut) -> int` returning `0` or a packed fault code of the owner's domain, with the invariant id and two ints written to the caller-owned `out` (no allocation; a Class A shape in the sense of ADR-0003 § 5). `<Owner>VerifierViews` is a plain `RefCounted` holding the read-view facades the check needs (SIM views only, never a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block), built by the composition root at `setup`. The block's `post_restore` does `var rc := X.verify_restore(views, out); if rc != 0: ctx.fault(rc, out.detail()); return ctx.complete()`. The same function is reused unchanged by runtime assertions (Assembly's release subset, § 5.4). Fault names follow `<DOMAIN>_RESTORE_<REASON>` for a `restore` check and `<DOMAIN>_VERIFY_<INV>` for a cross-block `post_restore` check, both in the owner's static domain (ADR-0003 § 6).

246	### 6. The binding rebuild (half (b))
247	
248	**6.1 Registration.** A block that owns an entity a PlayerId acts as registers `BlockDescriptor.binding_source` at `BOOTING` (ADR-0003 § 2; the binding source is this field only). At the MVP: `body.state` (`seat_bindings() -> [(seat, actor_id)]`, ascending seat, `SEAT` rows only, derived per call; TR-shipbody-030) and `emitter.state` (`beam_bindings() -> [(player_id, beam_id)]`, ascending `player_id`, pure read; TR-emitter-009). `controller.state` is not a source: it stores the PlayerId and resolves the actor through Body (ADR-0019 § 2.1).
249	
250	**6.2 Payload form.** `binding_source(ctx: SnapshotContext) -> CompletionToken` delivers through `ctx.put(pairs)` one **flat `PackedInt64Array`** `[player_id_0, entity_id_0, player_id_1, entity_id_1, ...]`, strictly ascending by `(player_id, entity_id)`, so no per-pair `Array` is allocated. The callable is a pure read: it receives no `WriteScope` and runs after every `post_restore`, so it reads rebuilt state.
251	
252	**6.3 The rebuild.** At R6/N6, after the verdict and as the last step of every pass, the kernel iterates `bind_order` (ascending **`String(block_id)`** of the source, the comparison of probe P1; a `StringName` comparison or `sort()` is forbidden, lint RST-01) and for each source: calls it, validates the array (even length; `player_id >= 1`; strictly ascending), and binds each pair as `player_id -> (source block, entity_id)` into the `PlayerBindings` object (ADR-0002 § 4). A key `(source block, entity_id)` delivered for two different PlayerIds, or the same `(player_id, source, entity_id)` delivered twice, or a malformed array, or a source that called `ctx.fault` or returned without the token, is `BINDING_REBUILD_CONFLICT` (domain 0 code 3) with detail `{reason, source, player_id, entity_id}` where `reason` is one of `CONFLICT_OWNER`, `DUPLICATE_TRIPLE`, `SHAPE`, `ORDER`, `PLAYER_RANGE`, `SOURCE_FAULT`. Equal entity numbers from two sources (Body actor 1, Emitter beam 1) are two keys and never conflict; comparisons are within one source. The rebuild is not a control-plane request and no command can interleave (the pass is one boundary service).
253	
254	**6.4 Consequences.** Half (b) is never saved, never read from the payload and never written by a block (TR-saveload-037); the first `RUNNING` tick passes the authority check for PlayerId 1 against `(body.state, avatar actor)` and `(emitter.state, beam)` (KRN-RST-06 submits an `OWNED_BY_ISSUER` command on tick 1 of a restored run); Body's `post_restore` does not rebuild it (TR-shipbody-010); a fault leaves half (b) empty (§ 1.3). Half (a) (`peer_id -> PlayerId`) is never touched by a pass.

256	### 7. Pass timing and diagnostics
257	
258	Per block and stage the kernel records `t_restore(b)` and `t_post(b)` through the injected `Clock` port (`now_us()`, ADR-0006 § Constraints, SIM-02 applies: logged, never branched on), plus `t_verdict` and `t_rebind`, into the `LoadTiming` diagnostics record. The sum is the `loading_ms` of the kernel GDD's load-budget formula; the per-owner figures (Graph `restore` plus `post_restore` at most 2 ms; the MVP world at most 3 ms with a 10 ms ceiling, TR-lsg-036) are checked by KRN-RST-14 against the registry names `LOADING_TARGET_MS` and the Graph's, reported and never a cut-off. A pass above its owner's figure is a diagnostic, like `STEP_BUDGET_MS`.
259	
260	### 8. Tests that make the rules falsifiable
261	
262	- **Order-permutation (G4) test, KRN-RST-05.** For a fixed seeded world, snapshot at tick `T`, then restore into fresh kernels whose `RestorePlan` is replaced by each of at least four **other valid linear extensions** of the same DAG (smallest id first, largest id first, reverse registration, and a seeded shuffle of ready lists), run 120 ticks each, and compare the per-tick `state_hash` trace and a battery of read-view answers (`lit`, `top_emitter`, `room_at`, `served_pm`, door-leaf rects, seat bindings) with the uninterrupted run. A block that read a non-predecessor's unbuilt derived state, or depended on the wiring order, fails here.
263	- **Reconciliation symmetry, KRN-RST-11** (§ 4.3), per owner that defers a reconcile.
264	- **Fault ladder, KRN-RST-04.** For every stage and every block of the MVP fixture a stub injects `ctx.fault`; the test asserts the recorded `LoadFailure`, that no later callable ran, that no tick, `ALL` batch or `load_seq` increment happened, that `FAULTED` rejects commands and snapshots, and that a following good `request_restore` matches a fresh kernel.
265	- **Lint pack RST** (proposed to ADR-0010 § 6 as a new pack): **RST-01** (error, `src/kernel`, `src/save`, `src/shared`): `<`, `>` or `.sort()` applied to a `StringName` operand or an `Array[StringName]`, outside the one helper `BlockIdOrder.less(a: StringName, b: StringName)` which compares `String(a) < String(b)`. **RST-02** (error, `src/sim`): a file named `*_restore.gd` or `*_verify.gd` references no other block's mutator class (the class map of ADR-0010 § 2.1 lists them); the run-time fence is the `RESTORE` scope. **RST-03** (error, whole `src/`): `init_world(` is called only from `src/kernel/` (the pass driver); owners define it and never call it. A fourth rule is a test, not a lint: **RST-04** every registered persisted block has a `FixtureFactory` entry (§ 9).
266	
267	### 9. Idempotence, fixtures and `REBASE_BLOCKS`
268	
269	**9.1 Rule.** Every persisted block is restore-idempotent: `snapshot -> encode -> decode -> restore -> snapshot` yields equal canonical bytes (ADR-0006 § 2.2). The way to get there is **normalise in `snapshot()`, not in `post_restore`**: a transient field the block would clear on restore (an in-progress channel, a door attempt, a pending completion, a controller ramp) is written in its cleared form by `snapshot()` while the live block keeps its value, so the restore reproduces the saved bytes exactly and `post_restore` has nothing to write. Assembly (`pending` written NONE, TR-assembly-012) and the Controller (PC-17) already do this.
270	
271	**9.2 `FixtureFactory` and the generic harness (TR-saveload-034).** Each persisted block registers, in the test tree only, a `FixtureFactory` with `empty() -> Dictionary` (equal to its `default_state` payload), `typical(seed) -> Dictionary` and `extreme(seed) -> Dictionary` (caps reached, tombstones present, counters near limits). `tests/unit/restore/idempotence_test.gd` **enumerates the registry** (never a hand list), and for every persisted block and fixture asserts the round trip, that `default_state` equals `empty()`, and that the block restores from its own `default_state` payload. A persisted block without a factory fails RST-04.
272	
273	**9.3 `REBASE_BLOCKS` is a checked list, not a convention.** The build constant `REBASE_BLOCKS` (Save/Load, SL-12) is a committed array in `src/save/` with one data row per member in `tests/fixtures/rebase_blocks.json`: `{block_id, owner_adr, reason, exit}`. CI fails if (a) a block is idempotent under § 9.2 but listed (a stale entry) or non-idempotent but not listed; (b) a build tagged for an outside release has a non-empty list. The gate flips with the same project-level `SHIPPED` decision as ADR-0007's id ledgers and ADR-0006 § 2.6. **Interim members at the MVP: `interaction.state`**, whose `post_restore` drops in-progress channels, door attempts and `last_result` and resolves a RESERVED FULL-job part (IA-36; OQ-39). Its exit is ADR-0020's: move those clears into `snapshot()` (the saved payload carries the dropped form and the resolved part), after which `post_restore` only rebuilds `W`. An older, un-normalised payload is still handled by a tolerant restore, as a migration. No other MVP block needs the list: `layout.state`'s geometry-hash rewrite (ADR-0013 § 10 drift policy) occurs only on a content change and is accepted as a REBASED case, not a standing member.
274	
275	### 10. Resource lifetime across passes (TR-light-037, this ADR's half)
276	
277	A pass must leave the object, node and orphan-node counts where the previous pass left them: scratch objects are acyclic and dropped at the end of the owner's `restore`; contexts, scopes, tokens and read-view facades are the kernel's and the owners' long-lived objects, re-armed rather than rebuilt (ADR-0003 § 3, § 7); `restore` copies into the existing block, so no facade or pool handle goes stale. KRN-RST-10 alternates `request_restore` and `request_new_game` 100 times on the headless kernel and asserts that `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT`, `OBJECT_NODE_COUNT` and `OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT` after cycle *n* equal those after cycle 1 (probe P4: all three monitors are readable headless; probe P3: a retained cycle is detected). ADR-0028 extends the same loop with the build, body-swap and render-texture legs and the light and occluder pools; this ADR guarantees only that the pass itself leaks nothing.

341	### Implementation Guidelines
342	- **Must** drive restore, `post_restore`, `default_state` and `init_world` from the one compiled `RestorePlan`; **must never** iterate a `Dictionary` or the registry's insertion order to order them.
343	- **Must** compare and sort block ids as `String` through `BlockIdOrder.less`; **must never** apply `<`, `>` or `.sort()` to `StringName` values (probe P1).
344	- **Must** run the pre-check over the whole payload before any owner callable or kernel write; **must never** call a `restore()` on the strength of a partially checked payload.
345	- **Must** stop the pass at the first fault and enter `FAULTED`; **must never** continue to later blocks, deliver an `ALL` batch, increment `load_seq`, or accept a snapshot after a faulted pass.
346	- **Must** apply a `default_state` payload through the block's own `restore`; **must never** let `default_state` write the live block directly.
347	- **Must** make `post_restore` rebuild derived members only (§ 4.2); **must never** clamp, prune, repair, default or write a persisted value or another block from it, except a `REBASE_BLOCKS` member's documented normalisation.
348	- **Must** express every after-load fix-up as the owner's ordinary hook rule that is a no-op on consistent state (§ 4.3); **must never** key behaviour on "first run after restore".
349	- **Must** read only Tier S of non-predecessors and only closure predecessors in `restore`; **must** tag every read-view method S or D in its doc comment.
350	- **Must** put verifier code in `*_verify.gd` as a pure `static` function returning 0 or a packed code and reuse it for runtime assertions; **must never** put a cross-block rule in the kernel.
351	- **Must** deliver binding pairs as a strictly ascending flat `PackedInt64Array` from a pure read; **must never** write the binding table, rebuild it from a block, or save it.
352	- **Must** keep restore scratch objects free of reference cycles and drop them before `restore` returns.
353	- **Must** register a `FixtureFactory` for every persisted block and keep `REBASE_BLOCKS` equal to the measured non-idempotent set.
354	- **Must never** call `init_world` outside the pass driver, or in a restore pass.

356	## Alternatives Considered
357	
358	### Alternative 1: `post_restore` order follows registration order, or is unordered
359	- **Description**: Run every `restore` in DAG order but every `post_restore` in registration order (or in no stated order, the Layout GDD's "informational only" reading), relying on each owner's self-heal.
360	- **Pros**: Nothing new to specify; works if no block reads another's derived state.
361	- **Cons**: Emitter Open Question 26 and ADR-0019 need the order; correctness of the Emitter's cold build for open doors would rest on a version-bump self-heal only; the dependency would be invisible and break on a wiring change.
362	- **Rejection Reason**: The DAG already exists and the order is free; stating it makes the dependency declared and testable (§ 8).
363	
364	### Alternative 2: Tie-break by `String(block_id)` instead of registration index
365	- **Description**: Kahn with the smallest `block_id` taken first, so the order is a function of the descriptors alone and does not depend on the composition root's wiring.
366	- **Pros**: Independent of wiring order; reproducible from a saved registry list.
367	- **Cons**: A second ordering algorithm beside ADR-0003 § 8's hook sort; the architecture's registration order (Layout, Graph, Body, ...) is already the natural dependency order, so the result is less intuitive to print and review.
368	- **Rejection Reason**: One algorithm and one total order for hooks and restore is easier to hold in a reviewer's head; the cost (order changes when wiring changes) is exactly what KRN-RST-05 detects. The binding walk still uses `String(block_id)` because its order is externally visible in the conflict report.
369	
370	### Alternative 3: A separate kernel verification stage with registered verifier callables
371	- **Description**: After R4 the kernel runs a list of `VerifierDescriptor` callables registered at `BOOTING`, so every verifier sees every block fully rebuilt.
372	- **Pros**: A verifier never reads a half-built block; one place names the first failing invariant; the Assembly verifier could live outside `post_restore`.
373	- **Cons**: A new registrar surface and descriptor (an ADR-0003 change); the TR rows say the checks run in `post_restore`; at the MVP every cross-block check reads Tier S or a predecessor, so the benefit is not yet needed.
374	- **Rejection Reason**: Not needed now; kept as the second move of § 5.6 if a verifier ever needs a non-predecessor's derived state.
375	
376	### Alternative 4: Validate every block first, then commit every block (kernel-level two-phase)
377	- **Description**: Add a `validate_restore(data, ctx)` callable; run it for all blocks, and only if all pass call `restore`, so an owner failure leaves the pre-restore world intact.
378	- **Pros**: Pre-restore state survives any `restore` failure, not only the pre-check.
379	- **Cons**: A new mandatory descriptor field and double decode cost; cross-block validations (Body's liveness check against Layout's *restored* state, V5) cannot run before Layout is committed; no MVP caller can use an intact old world.
380	- **Rejection Reason**: The benefit has no caller (both callers discard the live world) and the cross-block checks make it impractical; the per-block two-phase of ADR-0006 plus the pre-check covers what can be covered.
381	
382	### Alternative 5: Revert on failure from a pre-restore in-memory snapshot
383	- **Description**: Capture the live `WORLD` blocks before each pass and restore them if the pass faults.
384	- **Pros**: A failed load leaves the player in their world.
385	- **Cons**: A second restore pass that can itself fail; double cost on every load; contradicts the kernel GDD's "out of scope"; the Continue path has no live world to return to.
386	- **Rejection Reason**: § 1.4. Fallback to the next generation (a new pass) is Save/Load's mechanism.
387	
388	### Alternative 6: Widen the `RESTORE` scope so `post_restore` may write predecessor blocks
389	- **Description**: Let `post_restore(X)` open the blocks in X's `restore_after` closure, so Interaction's `post_restore` can re-register subjects with the Emitter as IA-36 words it.
390	- **Pros**: Matches the wording of TR-interact-016 literally.
391	- **Cons**: Breaks ADR-0003 § 4 ("the restoring block only"); makes "post_restore changes only derived state" unprovable; the persisted subject registrations make the re-registration redundant; a hash-visible cross-block write at load invites G4 divergences.
392	- **Rejection Reason**: Redundant for a consistent save and unsafe for an inconsistent one; the drift is detected in `post_restore` and repaired by the ordinary hook (§ 4.3). The cost is a GDD sync (below). If the owners later insist, the change is one row of ADR-0003 § 4 and a foundation ask, not a redesign.
393	
394	### Alternative 7: Clamp in `post_restore` for the lowered `stock_cap` case
395	- **Description**: Run the Graph's stock reconcile in `post_restore` (ADR-0011 Open Question 2's alternative).
396	- **Pros**: The first run starts from an already reconciled store.
397	- **Cons**: The restore stops being byte-identical (`snapshot(restore(x)) != x`), forces a REBASED cause 4/5 entry in ADR-0006, and makes `post_restore` a writer of persisted state, which § 4.2 forbids for everyone.
398	- **Rejection Reason**: Phase 0 does the same arithmetic as any step, keeps K-4 at `MATCH`, and closes TR-itemdb-033 without touching the post_restore rule.
399	
400	### Alternative 8: Order binding sources by the DAG or by registration index
401	- **Description**: Rebuild half (b) by walking `post_order` instead of ascending `block_id`.
402	- **Pros**: One order for everything.
403	- **Cons**: TR-cmd-013 states ascending `block_id`; the result is order-independent except for which conflict is reported first, and a block-id order is stable across wiring changes.
404	- **Rejection Reason**: Follow the GDD; use `String` comparison explicitly (probe P1).

406	## Consequences
407	
408	### Positive
409	- One sequence for restore and one for new game, each with a named failure state; the "faulted `LOADING` never plays" guarantee is stated and tested.
410	- `post_restore` order is declared data; the Emitter's cold build no longer depends on a self-heal, and any hidden dependency is caught by the permutation test.
411	- The post_restore write policy is one table every owner can check; deferred fix-ups become ordinary hook rules, so G4 holds by construction.
412	- Verifiers are listed once, owned by their blocks, reused at runtime, and the first failure is deterministic (fuzzable).
413	- The `REBASE_BLOCKS` exit is a CI gate with a named owner, not a convention.
414	- A real engine trap (StringName ordering) is found, fenced by a lint and a helper, and tested.
415	
416	### Negative
417	- Five foundation changes (three kernel codes, two pass codes, an outcome record) and one new lint pack are asked of ADR-0003, ADR-0002 and ADR-0010.
418	- Interaction must change its design from "re-register at `post_restore`" to "detect at `post_restore`, repair in the hook", and move its normalisation into `snapshot()` before the first outside build.
419	- The pass stops at the first fault, so a corrupt save reports one problem at a time.
420	- A failed load cannot return the player to the pre-load world; the fallback is another generation.
421	- The permutation test multiplies the cost of every restore-affecting change in CI.
422	
423	## Risks
424	- **R1: a block quietly depends on registration order.** Mitigation: KRN-RST-05 across at least four linear extensions on the MVP fixture, run on every push; a failing hash trace names the first diverging tick and block.
425	- **R2: Tier S/Tier D tags drift from the code.** Mitigation: the tags are doc comments read by a lint of the same pack and printed by the Debug Overlay; the permutation test is the semantic check. Residual risk is accepted until the lint pack is built.
426	- **R3: a deferred reconcile is not a no-op in the uninterrupted run.** Mitigation: KRN-RST-11 compares 600 ticks per owner; an owner that cannot make its fix-up idempotent files an ADR amendment before its story closes.
427	- **R4: the `kernel.clock` payload entry's shape (`tick_rate`) is not yet fixed by ADR-0006.** Mitigation: Open Question 2 and a foundation ask; until settled the `TICK_RATE_MISMATCH` pre-check cannot run on a payload without it.
428	- **R5: GDScript cost of a full pass is unmeasured** (Verification 2). Mitigation: it is a logged diagnostic, not a gate; S1 and SAVE-WRK-1-SLICE decide whether any rung is needed.
429	- **R6: `sanity.perception` has no declared `restore_after`.** Mitigation: assumed edges in § 2.4; if ADR-0025 declares none it can run before the blocks it rebuilds from. Open Question 1.
430	- **R7: a future PROFILE block's cold-open ordering is untested** at zero MVP blocks. Mitigation: the plan already visits `PROFILE` blocks in the cold-open pass; a story builds the test with the first PROFILE block.
431	- **R8: the proposed verifier V11 (one-holder) is outside Interaction's closed reason list.** Mitigation: it is marked proposed; accept or drop it with ADR-0020 (Open Question 3).

470	## Performance Implications
471	- **CPU**: One-time DAG compile at the freeze, O(n²) over at most `MAX_BLOCKS` blocks. A pass is the sum of the owners' `restore` and `post_restore` plus a handful of kernel steps (about two `Callable.call` per block, three stages); owner figures are the Graph's `restore` plus `post_restore` at most 2 ms and the MVP world at most 3 ms with a 10 ms ceiling (TR-lsg-036), all UNVERIFIED on a release export (S1, SAVE-WRK-1-SLICE). The pass is one boundary service and may exceed a frame; the Pipeline holds the black quad (`LOADING_TARGET_MS`, `t_hold_pad`). The binding rebuild is O(sources x players) with players at most 4. Assembly's release verifier subset is its own allocation (`verifier_release`).
472	- **Memory**: `RestorePlan` is five `PackedInt32Array`s of at most `MAX_BLOCKS`; scratch objects are transient and acyclic; no new retained structure.
473	- **Load Time**: Inside `loading_ms` of the kernel GDD; pre-check and file decode are Save/Load's and off the main thread when hot.
474	- **Network**: None. The order is a pure function of registration data, so a co-op guest running the same build restores identically (VS-B).

481	- **KRN-RST-02** Stage trace: recorded stubs show R0..R7 and N0..N7 in order, `post_restore` in the same order as `restore`, `init_world` only in N4 and never in a restore.

488	- **KRN-RST-09** Idempotence over the enumerated registry and `FixtureFactory` set; `REBASE_BLOCKS` equals the measured set.

490	- **KRN-RST-11** Reconciliation symmetry per deferring owner.

73	### 2. A block is a `RefCounted` held by its owner; the kernel holds descriptors
74	
75	The kernel never stores or inspects block data. It stores descriptors and calls the owner's callables. The owner's block object is a `RefCounted` with typed fields (packed arrays for struct-of-arrays state), never a `Resource` or `Node`. **`restore` copies into the existing block object and never replaces it**, because read views are long-lived facades over that object (§ 7); a test restores a block and checks its facade sees the restored values.
76	
77	**Snapshot payload contract** *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07; ADR-0005 § 5.3, ADR-0006)*: every packed array an owner puts in a `snapshot` payload is a **duplicate** (`PackedXArray.duplicate()` or a freshly built array), never a live reference to the block's own array. The kernel reads the payload after `snapshot` returns, hashes it outside SAVING (ADR-0005) and may hold it while the owner keeps writing; a live reference would let a later mutator change a payload already encoded or queued for the writer. `restore` likewise copies out of `data` and keeps no reference into it. A test mutates the block after `snapshot` and checks the payload unchanged.
78	
79	Every field is mandatory unless marked optional; a missing field fails boot naming the descriptor (CR-6: no silent defaults). GDScript reserves `class` as a keyword, so the GDD's `class` field is `block_class` in code.
80	
81	**`BlockDescriptor`**

84	|---|---|---|
85	| `block_id` | `StringName` | Unique, namespaced (e.g. `&"graph.state"`) |
86	| `owner_name` | `StringName` | Registering system, for diagnostics |
87	| `schema_version` | `int` | Bumped on any serialised-shape change |
88	| `supported_versions` | `PackedInt32Array` | Versions `restore` accepts |
89	| `block_class` | `int` enum `SIM` / `PERCEPTION_OUT` | CR-12 |
90	| `persist` | `bool` | false = derived, rebuilt after load |
91	| `persist_scope` | `int` enum `WORLD` / `PROFILE` | Required when `persist` |
92	| `scope` | `int` enum `SHARED` / `PER_PLAYER` | PER_PLAYER keyed by PlayerId |

94	| `interpolated` | `bool` | Kernel runs `commit_baseline` at P4 |

A reference across blocks is the pair `(block_id, entity_id)`, and `(source block_id, entity_id)` is the key form used by the binding sources (ADR-0002 § 4, binding table). A block's counter lives inside the block and is part of its snapshot payload, so a restore returns it to the saved value.

123	### 3. Contexts: reused, re-armed per call, non-re-entrant
124	
125	Every kernel-invoked callable receives a context as its last argument and reports only through it. The kernel allocates **one context object per kind at boot and re-arms it before every call**; nothing is allocated per call. *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07; ADR-0005 § 5.3.)* **One further kernel-internal `SnapshotContext`** serves hash reads (`block_hash`, `state_hash`) made **outside `SAVING`**, so a hash read never re-arms the context a save capture or a restore is using. It carries its own re-entrancy flag: a `block_hash` call made from inside a `snapshot` call (which would arm the same context twice) is a `CONTEXT_REENTRY` violation and returns a not-ok result, never a hash. It is a kernel member under H1 `kernel_state` and is never exposed to owners.
126	
127	```gdscript
128	class_name CallContext extends RefCounted          # base; subclasses add methods and override none
129	var completed: bool
130	var epoch: int
131	var faulted: bool:                                  # true if fault() was called here OR on the linked WriteScope
132		get: return _faulted or (_scope != null and _scope.faulted)
133	func put(payload: Variant) -> void                  # snapshot / default_state / read_view / empty_view / binding_source
134	func fault(code: int, detail: Dictionary = EMPTY_DETAIL) -> void   # packed FAULT_CODE (§ 6); EMPTY_DETAIL is shared and never mutated
135	func complete() -> CompletionToken                  # sets completed, stamps the armed token's epoch, returns it
136	
137	class_name ValidateContext extends CallContext      # validate: read-only
138	func ok() -> void                                   # first outcome stands; a second is CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME
139	func reject(reason: StringName) -> void             # -> Rejected(VALIDATION_FAILED(reason))
140	
141	class_name TickContext extends CallContext          # shared base of the two contexts that may submit
142	var tick: int
143	func submit_system(type: StringName, payload: Dictionary, dedupe_key: Variant = null) -> void
144	func has_pending(type: StringName, dedupe_key: Variant = null) -> bool
145	class_name ApplyContext extends TickContext         # apply
146	class_name HookContext extends TickContext          # step hooks; adds hook_id
147	class_name SnapshotContext extends CallContext      # snapshot, restore, post_restore, default_state, init_world,
148	                                                    # commit_baseline, snap_baseline, binding_source, read_view, empty_view
149	class_name NotifyContext extends CallContext        # subscriber, result and control-outcome handlers (a fault is counted, never fatal)
150	                                                    # file: src/kernel/facets/notify_context.gd (ADR-0010 § 1.1, TD-01): a presenter handler must name it
151	```
152	
153	`submit_system` exists only on `TickContext`, so `validate` cannot submit (it receives a `ValidateContext`) and no "refused call" path is needed.
154	
155	**Placement of `NotifyContext`** *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-01)*: the subscriber, result and control-outcome handler context lives in `src/kernel/facets/` with `CompletionToken`, `ChangeBatch`, `NotifyEvent` and the other types a presenter must name (ADR-0010 § 1.1, ADR-0004 placement table), because a presenter's handler signature `(batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken` has to compile in `src/presentation/`. The tick-phase contexts (`CallContext`, `ValidateContext`, `ApplyContext`, `HookContext`, `SnapshotContext`) stay in kernel core and are on ADR-0010's presentation deny list; there is no `*Context` glob.
156	
157	**Re-arm list.** Before each call the kernel, in one step: increments `epoch`; sets `completed = false`, `_faulted = false`, the outcome (`ok`/`reject`) to none, the `put` payload to none and the fault detail to `EMPTY_DETAIL`; links the context to the call's scope (or to none); and sets a re-entrancy flag. After the call it clears the flag. A call made while the flag is set is a `CONTEXT_REENTRY` violation; the MVP needs one context per kind, because a hook's `submit_system` queues and does not call another kernel callable synchronously.
158	
159	**The token check.** The kernel keeps one `CompletionToken` per context object. `complete()` sets `completed = true`, writes the current epoch into the token and returns it. After the call the kernel accepts the result only if the returned value **is** that token (identity), `token.epoch == ctx.epoch` and `ctx.completed` is true. The kernel holds the call result as a `Variant` and tests identity with `is_same()`, so a coroutine state returned by an owner that hit `await` fails the check like any other non-token value. Anything else, including `null`, a type default, a coroutine state or a token kept from an earlier call, is `fault(INCOMPLETE)` (or, for a handler or a view callable, a recorded `INCOMPLETE` diagnostic without a fault). The check does not depend on what an aborted call returns (Verification 1). One hole is closed by rule: an owner that aborted *after* `complete()` ran would read as success, so `return ctx.complete()` is the **last statement** and nothing follows `complete()` in the same expression (a CI check). A `validate` that calls neither `ok()` nor `reject()` is `Faulted(NO_OUTCOME)`. This satisfies the GDD's "fresh `ctx.token`" guarantee without allocating; the GDD wording is amended (§ GDD sync).

161	### 4. `WriteScope`: reused, the only way to write and to mark dirty
162	
163	```gdscript
164	class_name WriteScope extends RefCounted
165	enum Phase { CLOSED, APPLY, HOOK, PAUSED_APPLY, INIT, RESTORE }
166	var phase: Phase
167	var faulted: bool                                   # set by fault(); closes the scope (fail-closed)
168	func open_for(block_id: StringName) -> bool         # see the table below
169	func mark_dirty(block_id: StringName, key: int) -> void   # key layout: ADR-0004 § 3
170	func emit_event(block_id: StringName, kind: int, a0: int = 0, a1: int = 0, a2: int = 0, a3: int = 0, a4: int = 0, a5: int = 0) -> void   # P5 event record; ADR-0004 § 5
171	func has_opened(block_index: int) -> bool           # true from the first granted open_for of that block until the scope is re-armed (ADR-0005 § 5.3)
172	func fault(code: int, detail: Dictionary = EMPTY_DETAIL) -> void
173	```
174	
175	The kernel allocates the scope objects once and re-arms them (phase, writable set, `faulted = false`, dirty buffer) per use, like the contexts.
176	
177	| Phase | When | `open_for(block)` true for |
178	|---|---|---|
179	| `APPLY` | P2 `apply` of one command (`RUNNING`) | any block (cross-block applies call other owners' published mutators) |
180	| `PAUSED_APPLY` | the paused service cycle | only blocks in the command type's `writes_blocks` (GDD CR-16) |
181	| `HOOK` | one P3 hook run | any block |
182	| `INIT` | new-game construction in `LOADING`: all `init_world` steps share one `INIT` scope, before `post_restore` (CR-18) | any block |
183	| `RESTORE` | an owner's `restore` / `post_restore` that uses its own mutators | the restoring block only |
184	| `CLOSED` | everything else, and after the first `fault` | nothing |
185	
186	`init_world` therefore receives the scope: `init_world(world_seed: int, scope: WriteScope, ctx: SnapshotContext)`, and Web Map's `init_world` passes it to Layout `build_section`, Emitter `instantiate_section_emitters` and Interaction `sync_section` (architecture § Initialisation order step 6). **Dirty keys marked in `INIT` and `RESTORE` scopes are discarded**: on the `LOADING → RUNNING` transition the kernel delivers one `ALL` batch per block instead (the GDD's "one ALL then silence"), which is what the PROJECTOR needs after a new game or a load; ADR-0004 defines that delivery.
187	
188	`open_for` returning false writes nothing, counts `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` and reports a violation (CR-9) — except when the scope is closed because of an earlier fault, which is not counted again. Dirty keys are marked **only** through `scope.mark_dirty` inside the mutator that changed the data, never from a setter. The debug-build check that catches a missed mark is ADR-0004 § 7 (it compares a block's hash with the kernel's `touch_serial` and with whether any key was marked, for blocks that do not declare `quiet_writes_allowed`); this ADR no longer states the rule. `emit_event` follows the same scope rules as `mark_dirty`: it needs an open block and its records are discarded in `INIT`, `RESTORE` and `CLOSED` (ADR-0004 § 5). `has_opened` is a pure read used by the kernel's hash path (ADR-0005 § 5.3): it never opens anything and never counts a violation. `writes_blocks` is enforced in `PAUSED_APPLY` as the GDD requires; under `STRICT_DEBUG` it is also checked during `RUNNING`, where a write to a block outside `writes_blocks` is a `WRITES_BLOCKS_UNDECLARED` violation, to catch undeclared cross-block writes early.
189	
190	### 5. Mutators: status returns, fail-closed, no rollback
191	
192	**Status values**: `OK = 0`; `REFUSED = 1` (the scope was not open for this block: a counted violation, **not** a fault, and never escalated by the caller); a **negative** value is `-fault_code` (a defect the mutator detected; it has also called `scope.fault`).
193	
194	- **Class A** (validate-then-apply): a pure `check_*(views, args) -> StringName` (`&""` = OK) takes read views only; the matching mutator `name(scope, args, out) -> int` is infallible once its check passed. A mutator that produces data (a new id, a `{seam_id, opening_ids}` record) writes it into a **caller-owned `out` object** passed in, so the return value is always the status. Example: `weld_join(scope: WriteScope, plan: JoinPlan, out: WeldResult) -> int`.
195	- **Class B** (clamp, never reject): `name(scope, args) -> void`; it clamps out-of-range input and no-ops on a stale id; it still begins with `scope.open_for`.
196	
197	**Fail-closed.** The first `scope.fault` sets `scope.faulted`, which closes the scope: every later `open_for` on it is false (not counted again), so later mutators in the same apply write nothing and the dev-build diagnostics show the blocks exactly as they were at the fault. `ctx.faulted` includes the scope's flag (§ 3). **Fail-closed never depends on an engine error aborting the callee** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — architecture review)*: a release build may log a script error and continue. It is carried by the explicit paths only — mutator status checks, `scope.fault` and the closed scope — with the `STRICT_DEBUG` checks and ADR-0004's debug-build missed-mark hash as backstops. An engine error that a release build swallows and that no mutator detects is outside what the kernel can see; KRN-CTX-06 documents it rather than claims it.
198	
199	**Caller procedure.** After every Class A call the caller checks the status. On `REFUSED` or a negative status it returns `ctx.complete()` at once: no further mutator calls and no second `ctx.fault` (the scope fault already counts). The kernel reads `ctx.faulted` after the callable returns.
200	
201	**No rollback.** A fault leaves the blocks touched so far half-applied. This is acceptable because `FAULTED` is terminal until an explicit reload or new game (both rebuild every `WORLD` block) and the kernel never writes or autosaves over an existing save in `FAULTED` (GDD). Nothing here rules out OQ-15's alternative for the weld: ADR-0021 may snapshot the touched blocks before its apply and restore them on a fault, using the `snapshot` / `restore` callables this ADR defines.
202	
203	### 6. Fault codes: static domains, pre-packed constants
204	
205	A fault code is a positive `int`: `(DOMAIN_ID << 16) | local`, `local` in `1..65535`. **Domain ids are static**, so a code means the same thing in every build, log and fixture. Each system's `*_faults.gd` (a `class_name XFaults extends RefCounted` holding only constants, never instantiated, one class per file) declares `const DOMAIN_ID` and its codes **already packed** (`const NOT_IN_SCOPE: int = (DOMAIN_ID << 16) | 1`), plus `const NAMES: Array[StringName]` indexed by local code. It registers with `register_fault_domain(XFaults.DOMAIN_ID, owner_name, XFaults.NAMES)`; a duplicate or out-of-range id fails boot. A unit test checks each file's constants and `NAMES` agree. Codes are append-only and never reused. The kernel prints a fault as `domain.NAME`.

248	### 7. Read views: long-lived facades, issued by facet
249	
250	The kernel never hands out a live container. **Each owner's `read_view(ctx)` is called once, at the registry freeze**, and delivers a long-lived getter-only facade over its block object (typed scalar getters and caller-owned-buffer queries, so hot paths allocate nothing). Each owner also supplies **`empty_view(ctx)`**: a facade of the same class whose getters return neutral values (zero, false, empty) and whose `is_empty()` is true. This replaces the GDD's per-request `read_view` (§ GDD sync); it is valid only because `restore` copies into the existing block object (§ 2).
251	
252	`ReadViews` has two faces, issued as facets by the composition root (ADR-0001): **`SimViews`** (to `validate`, `apply` and hooks) and **`PresentationViews`** (to subscribers). Both have `get_view(block_id: StringName) -> Object` (never `get`: a method named `get` overrides the native `Object.get()`, which is a load-time parse error on 4.7.2, probed, and ADR-0010's `NATIVE_METHOD_OVERRIDE` rule), returning the owner's facade, which the caller casts to the owner's view class. For a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block, `SimViews.get_view` returns that block's typed `empty_view`, increments `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED` and reports a violation; `PresentationViews` returns the real facade (superseded for `PERCEPTION_OUT` by the two-face rule below). **Two faces of `PresentationViews`** *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07 item 10 and TD-08; ADR-0004 § 2 check 6, ADR-0009 § 1)*: `PresentationViews` carries a `perception_access: bool` that the composition root sets **once, at issue**, and presentation code cannot change. The **default face** (`perception_access == false`, every facet except the two below) answers `get_view(block_id)` for a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block with that block's typed `empty_view`, increments `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED` and reports a violation, exactly as `SimViews` does. The **perception face** (`perception_access == true`) returns the real facade. ADR-0009 § 1 fixes which facets carry the flag: the Perception Filter's `PresentationFacet` and the `DIAGNOSTIC` facets only. The same flag gates the subscription: ADR-0004 § 2 check 6 refuses, at subscribe time and in the kernel, a subscription to a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block with `SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED` unless the issuing facet carries `perception_access = true`. A `SIM`-class block is readable through either face. ADR-0024 owns only the Filter's query surface, not this rule.
253	
254	A fault in `read_view` or `empty_view` at the freeze is recorded and leaves the empty view in place; it never faults the kernel (CR-19(a)). Under `STRICT_DEBUG` the `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE` hashes SIM blocks per dispatch batch and around P5 (`TRIPWIRE_BUDGET_MS` 1.0 ms, full sweep every `TRIPWIRE_SWEEP_TICKS` 60), which catches a facade that leaks a mutable reference.
255	
256	### 8. Hooks: validated, sorted once, run from a precomputed schedule
257	
258	At the registry validation pass (an internal step of the boundary that serves the first `request_new_game` / `request_restore`, CR-6) the kernel:
259	
260	1. Fails boot on a duplicate id, an unknown `after` id, a cycle, `divisor < 1` or an `offset` outside `0..divisor-1` (an offset at or above its divisor would never fire).
261	2. Runs Kahn's algorithm with the ready list ordered by **registration index** (unique, so a total order; `hook_id` is the printed name), always taking the smallest ready index and never iterating a Dictionary.
262	3. Records a `STALE_EDGE_UNDECLARED` boot warning for any `after` edge between hooks that do not always run on the same tick unless it declares `tolerates_stale` (ruling R-8). The warning list must be empty at the end of every CI run (today it is not, because of `transit.step`, IC-11, until the Web Map GDD declares that edge).
263	4. **Compiles a schedule.** `C = lcm(all divisors)`, computed with a small integer `gcd`/`lcm` at boot (no builtin), guarding overflow; a `C` above `MAX_SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TICKS` (3,600) fails boot naming the divisor. For each residue `r` in `0..C-1` the schedule holds a `PackedInt32Array` of hook indices, in the total order, of the hooks with `r mod divisor == offset`. Each entry is built as a local array, filled completely, then assigned once and never mutated in place. With the MVP divisors (1, 5, 6, 12) `C` = 60. A tick does `schedule[T mod C]` and calls each index: no per-tick scan, and the schedule is data the Debug Overlay prints.
264	
265	**P3 budget semantics (IC-4).** Settled by the owner and recorded here: **P3 ≤ 2.0 ms P99 is the target; `STEP_BUDGET_MS` = 4 ms is an alarm threshold, not a target.** A P3 above 4 ms logs the slowest hooks; the tick completes; nothing aborts a hook mid-run.
266	
267	### 9. The kernel state machine is a data table
268	
269	States: `BOOTING`, `LOADING`, `RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, `SAVING`, `FAULTED`, `SHUTTING_DOWN`. The GDD's transition table is encoded as one constant table `(state, trigger) → target`, where a target may be the sentinel **`PRIOR`** (`SAVING` returns to the state it came from).
270	
271	- **Triggers** (closed): `request_pause`, `request_resume`, `request_snapshot`, `request_restore`, `request_new_game`, `request_shutdown`, `fault`, `capture_done`, `capture_error`, `load_done`, `load_failed`, `boot_validation_failed`, `teardown_done`.
272	- **Boot validation is not a trigger.** It is an internal step of the boundary that serves the first `request_new_game` / `request_restore` in `BOOTING`: on success the request proceeds (`BOOTING → LOADING` via the request's row); on failure the same boundary fires `boot_validation_failed` (`BOOTING → FAULTED`).
273	- **Deferral comes before the lookup.** A request made while an atomic step (`SAVING`, `LOADING`) is active is `DEFERRED` and evaluated, in arrival order, at the first boundary after the step, against the state that boundary finds. Only then is the table consulted; a pair not in the table is `IGNORED` with one invalid-transition diagnostics entry and no state change.
274	- **Seat binding is outside the table.** `request_bind_seat` / `request_unbind_seat` (ADR-0002) are non-transition requests: served at the boundary in `BOOTING`, `RUNNING` and `PAUSED` (`SERVED`), deferred during an atomic step, and `IGNORED` in `FAULTED` and `SHUTTING_DOWN`. They never change state.
275	- **Re-entry from `FAULTED` (closes OQ-5).** The kernel keeps `registry_valid: bool`, set true only by a passing validation pass. The `FAULTED` rows for `request_restore` and `request_new_game` apply only when `registry_valid`; a boot-failure `FAULTED` exits only through `request_shutdown`. A runtime fault keeps all three exits.
276	
277	The control-plane test KRN-STATE-01 is **generated from this table**: every row, every invalid pair, both kinds of `FAULTED`, and the non-transition requests, so a row added without a fixture row fails.
278	
279	### 10. Kernel members (the H1 allow-list)
280	
281	Everything this ADR adds to the kernel lives under the GDD's allow-listed groups, so the H1 lint stays a fixed list: **registries** (descriptors, the compiled schedule, the fault-domain table, `registry_valid`, the transition table); **kernel_state** (current state, the `PRIOR` return state, the reused contexts, tokens and scope objects); **diagnostics** (violation counters, boot warnings, the fault log).
282	
283	*(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07.)* The H1 **registries** group also holds, by name: `touch_serial` (a `PackedInt64Array` of `MAX_BLOCKS`, written by every granted `open_for`; ADR-0004 § 7), the **hash-cache arrays** (`{hash, enc_len, serial}` as three parallel `PackedInt64Array`s sized once at the freeze; ADR-0005 §§ 5.1, 5.2), the per-block key-space table (ADR-0004 § 3) and the subscription tables (ADR-0004 § 2). **kernel_state** also holds the kernel-internal hash `SnapshotContext` of § 3 and the `kernel.clock` below. The H1 lint's fixed list is extended by exactly these names.
284	
285	**The `kernel.clock` view.** `kernel.clock` is an H1 member owned by this ADR. It carries `(T, world_seed, restore_epoch)` and is exposed to modules and the composition root only as a read-only view (getters `tick()`, `world_seed()`, `restore_epoch()`; no setters). `T` advances only in the tick driver's boundary. **`world_seed`** is set before `INIT` (by `request_new_game`, or from the payload by `request_restore`) and does not change until the next new game or restore. **`restore_epoch`** is a `u32`, **read-only to owners, non-persisted and non-hashed**: it is in no state block, no canonical byte string, no `state_hash` and no snapshot header (ADR-0005 § 2.4). `request_restore` and `request_new_game` set it **before** the first `restore()` or `init_world`; Save/Load supplies the value and persists it in `slot_epoch.bin` (ADR-0006), but the kernel's copy is the only one the simulation can see. It is read only inside `RngFacet.draw_epoch` (ADR-0005 § 2.3); a lint forbids any other read in `src/sim/`.
286	
287	### Architecture Diagram

128:- **Header (JSON).** Every value that can reach 2^53 (`T`, `world_seed`, `state_hash`, each `block_state_hash`, `registry_epoch`) is an exact-width lowercase `hex64` string (16 chars): by ADR-0005 § 4.2 the **8 little-endian bytes of the `int`**. Save/Load calls `Hex64.encode(int)` and `Hex64.decode(String) -> Hex64Result` from `src/shared/det/` (`save` may import `shared`, ADR-0010) and defines **no 64-bit codec of its own** (TD-25). `Hex64.decode` first validates exactly 16 characters of `[0-9a-f]` with a plain loop (no regex, no engine error) and only then calls `hex_decode` and `decode_s64`, because `hex_decode` alone accepts uppercase (probe 18) and reports bad input by logging; `Hex64.encode` calls `resize(8)` before `encode_s64` (probe 17). `campaign_id` (128 bits) is an **opaque 32-character lowercase `[0-9a-f]` String that is never converted to an int**; the local helper `CampaignId.is_valid(s)` applies the same exact-width, lowercase pre-check by loop. `registry_epoch` is compared as a string and never decoded. **Never `String.hex_to_int`** (probed: it saturates to `INT64_MAX` with an error on 16 `f`s). A `world_seed` or hash with the top bit set therefore reads as a negative GDScript `int`; that is correct, not a bug, and every consumer compares as `int`. Header numbers that stay numbers (`format_version`, `schema_version`, `generation`, lengths, offsets, counts, `hash_algo`, `codec`, `tick_rate`, `restore_epoch`) arrive as `float` from the parser and must be integral and **strictly below 2^53** before conversion; a value of 2^53 or more is refused (probed: `9007199254740993` parses to `9007199254740992.0`, so the first ambiguous value is exactly 2^53, which the strict bound catches). The header text becomes a `String` through `get_string_from_utf8` only after the trailer passed, and is parsed with `JSON.new().parse(text)`, whose returned `Error` is checked; invalid UTF-8 behind a passing trailer is a tamper case that may log an engine `ERROR` (**UNVERIFIED**) and is accepted only in the re-hashed fuzz configuration, like the `bytes_to_var` case of § 1.2.
133:- **Quarantine reason is in the file name:** `quarantine/g<generation>_<REASON>_<k>.sav`, `REASON` in {`CORRUPT`, `RESTORE_FAILED`, `STALE_EPOCH`}. `gen_next` reads the generation from the name without opening the file (SL-19). No sidecar and no manifest entry: a manifest is a hint and a sidecar can be lost separately from the file.
163:- **A newer catalogue is INCOMPATIBLE, not owner-failed.** After step 12 (`tick_rate`) and before step 13 (the block table): a header `catalogue_version` greater than the running build's is `SL_PRECHECK_CATALOGUE_NEWER`, class INCOMPATIBLE, stop, no quarantine ("made by a newer build"). Without it, a downgrade would surface as `GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF` or `SUIT_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF`, an *owner-reported* failure that quarantines a good file after `QUARANTINE_AFTER_FAILURES` 2. A *lower or equal* version proceeds: owners resolve renamed defs through ADR-0007's alias path. `catalogue_hash` is diagnostic only and never gates a load.
167:**1.11 Fault domain 1 and the closed reason sets.** `src/save/save_load_faults.gd` (`class_name SaveLoadFaults extends RefCounted`, `const DOMAIN_ID: int = 1`, packed codes `(DOMAIN_ID << 16) | n`, and `const NAMES: Array[StringName] = [&"", &"PRECHECK_FILE_SHA_MISMATCH", ...]` indexed by the local code with index 0 = `&""`, the shape of ADR-0003's `GraphFaults.NAMES`) holds the closed sets `SL_PRECHECK_*`, `SL_WRITE_*`, `SL_LOAD_*`, `SL_VERIFY_*`, `SL_EPOCH_*`, `SL_QUIT_*`, `SL_NEW_GAME_*` and `SL_BOOT_*`, and Save/Load calls `register_fault_domain(1, &"save_load", NAMES)` in `BOOTING` through the BOOTING-only registrar facet that ADR-0003 gives a host service (limited to `register_fault_domain`; no block or hook registration), so diagnostics print `save_load.PRECHECK_FILE_SHA_MISMATCH`. **None of these faults the kernel**: a bad file, a failed write and a refused quit are values and diagnostics, and the kernel's own codes (`CAPTURE_ERROR` 7, `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE` 6, `RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BLOCK` 4, `TICK_RATE_MISMATCH` 5, all domain 0) are the unreachable backstops behind Save/Load's pre-check. Registering a domain is neither a block nor a hook, so TR-saveload-018 holds. Knob range and invariant failures (`SL_BOOT_KNOB_RANGE`, `SL_BOOT_KNOB_INVARIANT`) are **domain 2** content boot errors raised by the ADR-0007 `ScalarTable` machinery (TR-saveload-024 is ADR-0007's); only the cross-check of § 2.3, which needs the live registry, raises domain 1 `SL_BOOT_*`.
169:**1.12 The host API and what Save/Load may observe.** SL-21 as written: `new_game(world_seed)`, `continue_campaign()`, `save_and_quit()`, `cancel_held_close()`, read-only `campaign_info()`, `list_saves()`, `retire_campaign`, `delete_campaign`, and the host-local reads `save_status`, `fail_escalated`, `SaveInfo`, `restore_reason`, `restore_epoch` (diagnostic), `quit_held`, `quit_write_active`. No `save_now`, no `load(generation)` outside dev builds, no command registered (TR-saveload-023). Save/Load is a **polling control-plane caller, not a subscriber** (SL-13; TD-09): it holds a `ControlHandle` and a `save_load` facet of read views, subscribes to nothing and gets no end-of-tick callback and no sixth subscriber class. `SaveService.poll_frame()` (called by `SaveHost`, § 1.6) compares **monotonic counters** with the last values it saw; counters are chosen over level flags or `last_*_T` so that several events inside one catch-up frame are not lost. **The observation set (Save/Load's decision, owned here):** `kernel.clock`, `controller.state.loco_state` and `carry_ref` and `suit` `carried_id` (the SL-5 gate rows; TR-suit-035), `suit` `vitals_state`, `graph` failures, `attention.view`, Assembly's `ragged_breach_open()` and `last_shape_change_T()`, Interaction's `last_salvage_T()`, and the **conditional `web.state` read-view members `pod_arrived_seq: int` and `berthed_seq: int`**, recorded as a requirement on the Web Map ADR (Save/Load's half of TR-webmap-023). Until the Web Map ADR supplies them, the POD_ARRIVED and BERTHED triggers are absent and never fire (GDD rule: an event whose owner read is absent never fires). The last-seen copies are host-local and are re-read after a load, so a load never fires an autosave. ADR-0004 OQ-3 is closed from this side: Save/Load polls owner read views, there is no subscription class. Save/Load never reads a `PERCEPTION_OUT` view and never writes a block. It registers one `ControlHandle.set_outcome_handler` method `Callable` with the signature `(outcome: ControlOutcome, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken` that returns a token on every path, and uses it for the snapshot outcome (payload plus the hash data of § 1.1) and the K-4 verdict; `request_snapshot()` itself returns `void`.
179:- **Failure is reported through `ctx.fault(<OWNER>_RESTORE_*)`** with the owner's domain code and a named detail, never by return value and never by clamping; the kernel fires `load_failed` and Save/Load maps it to the `RESTORE_FAILED` class of SL-11. Owner GDDs that describe `(ok, reason, detail)` mean this (ADR-0003 sync, not this ADR's to change).
181:- A restore is idempotent: `snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` is canonical-byte identical except for the closed `REBASE_BLOCKS` list (SL-12), and the Graph's, Body's and Controller's tests prove it.
187:**2.5 `hash_algo` and `codec`.** `hash_algo` 2 names H64 (the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 via `HashingContext`, read little-endian, ratified by the GDD, owned by ADR-0005); 0 and 1 are reserved, never written (they are `hash_algo` ids, not hash values: no `H64` value is reserved as a sentinel, ADR-0005). An unsupported `hash_algo` skips the reproduction compare (`SL_VERIFY_ALGO_SKIPPED`, REBASED cause 4) so a kernel hash change is never a save-breaking event. `codec` 0 only.
193:**3.1 Ownership and storage.** Save/Load owns `restore_epoch`, an unsigned 32-bit integer (an `int` in `[0, 2^32 - 1]`) starting at 0 at `new_game` (SL-18); it has exactly one owner and registry entry. It lives in a per-slot **pair of side files**, `user://saves/<campaign_id>/slot_epoch_a.bin` and `slot_epoch_b.bin`, each **12 bytes: the epoch as `u32` LE, a sequence number `seq` as `u32` LE, then the CRC32 of those 8 bytes as `u32` LE** (the GDD / TR-saveload-020 format of `u32` plus CRC32 gains the `seq` field; GDD sync). The reader takes the valid file (size 12, CRC matches) with the higher `seq`; the writer always overwrites the **older** file in place (an invalid file, or the lower `seq`) with `seq = max + 1`, flushes, closes, re-reads and checks the CRC (that re-read is the `EPOCH_DURABLE` report). **No rename and no remove is involved**, so there is never an instant with no valid epoch file: a kill mid-write corrupts only the file being written and the other still holds the previous durable value. (A single file replaced by rename-over would, on Windows, probably be remove-then-rename, § 1.5, open a window in which the file is absent, and let the rebuild rule of § 3.4 yield `max(header copy) + 1`, which can be lower than an epoch already advanced, for example after two deaths with no autosave between them, replaying one set of threat draws; engine review E2.) `seq` saturates at 2^32 - 1, unreachable in practice because the epoch saturates first. `SlotEpoch.encode` calls `resize(12)` before any `encode_u32` (probe 17). **CRC32 is hand-rolled** (polynomial `0xEDB88320`, init and final XOR `0xFFFFFFFF`, bitwise, over 8 bytes): `PackedByteArray` has no `crc32` (probed), the scripted loop matched the standard check vector, its cost is of order microseconds, and a truncated hash was rejected as a gratuitous change to the GDD format. The vector `crc32("123456789") == 0xCBF43926` is a unit test. The files are in no generation, so no generation's bytes, trailer, `state_hash` or any key derived from them changes after `VERIFYING`; this is what makes SL-12's REBASED baseline key stable (R14). Each WORLD generation's header carries a **read-only write-time copy** (`restore_epoch`, an int below 2^32) used only by the rebuild rule of § 3.4; it is never rewritten.
203:**3.5 Reaching the sim.** `request_restore` and `request_new_game(world_seed, restore_epoch = 0)` pass the epoch as an argument; the kernel range-checks it (`RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE`, domain 0 code 6) and exposes it read-only, sim-visible and **non-persisted, non-hashed** in the `kernel.clock` read view as `(T, world_seed, restore_epoch)` before the first `restore()`; it is read only inside `RngFacet.draw_epoch` (ADR-0003, TD-07). The one derivation, `counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE * restore_epoch`, belongs to the kernel and ADR-0005 (`rng_derive_epoch`); Attention and Horror call it and never store the epoch (TR-attention-024, TR-horror-017). Determinism is defined given the pair: the same (save bytes, `restore_epoch`) replays identically, and tests pin the epoch. The phrase "excluded from the snapshot header" (TR-cmd-018) means *the kernel snapshot payload and every `H64`*: the **container** header carries the recovery copy of § 3.1, which is covered by the file trailer (file integrity) and by no state hash.
205:**3.6 Staging and hot copy.** Candidate selection (SL-8), the death-stub's one synchronous attempt per candidate and the newest and preceding **hot decoded copies** (SL-11) stand as written; the hot copies are held by Save/Load and are never handed to a worker (a retained alias of a handed-over buffer is forbidden, § 1.6). The payload handed to `request_restore` is built in memory by Save/Load (not decoded from one blob): `Dictionary` of `StringName block_id -> {&"schema_version": int, &"data": Dictionary}`, with `kernel.clock` included, `data` dictionaries marked read-only as a shallow convenience (`Dictionary.make_read_only()` is **shallow**, probe 14, so owners copy what they keep, OQ-53; a deep read-only snapshot, where wanted, is built by the owner from `duplicate(true)` at capture). The expected hash is passed as **two typed arguments**: `expected_state_hash: int` (the header `state_hash`) and `has_expected_hash: bool`, `false` when the file legitimately carries none (a release-build file that predates K-4: verdict `NONE`). No `null` and no `Variant` (ADR-0002, TD-05; OQ-B closed): `Variant` is banned in typed interfaces, passing `null` to an `int` parameter is a runtime error, and a legitimate `H64` of 0 exists, so no value is a sentinel.
319:- `restore_epoch` **must** be stored only in `slot_epoch_a.bin` / `slot_epoch_b.bin` (and as the read-only header copy), **must** never be inside a snapshot payload, an `H64` input or a block, and **must** reach the sim only as the `request_restore` / `request_new_game` argument and the `kernel.clock` view.
373:- **Cons**: Rewriting a verified file changes its trailer and every key derived from it (SL-12's REBASED baseline), races the write protocol, and loses the value when that generation is quarantined or the ring steps back.

171	### 2. Versioning and migration
172	
173	**2.1 Two levels, as SL-14.** `format_version` (container) is migrated by Save/Load; `schema_version` (per block) is migrated only by the owner inside `restore(data, stored_version, ctx)` as a chain of registered pure functions `(old Dictionary) -> new Dictionary`. Save/Load never rewrites block data. `min_reader_version` equals `format_version` on every write in the MVP. A migrated payload is **not written back** to the old file; the next autosave writes the new shape, so a downgrade-then-upgrade cannot half-migrate a file.
174	
175	**2.2 The block contract in ADR-0003 terms.** Reconciling SL-15 with the registered owner-callable contract (ADR-0003 § 1, registry `owner_callable_contract`): a persisted block registers `snapshot`, `restore`, `default_state` and `post_restore` as `Callable`s each returning `ctx.complete()`, with `supported_versions`, `persist_scope` and `restore_after` in its `BlockDescriptor`.
176	
177	- `snapshot(ctx)` calls `ctx.put(payload: Dictionary)`: a deep copy (no aliasing of live state, so the encode may later leave the main thread; packed arrays in the payload are duplicates, never live references, ADR-0003 snapshot contract), plain data per § 1.2, rows sorted by id, no derived caches, no object references, transient fields normalised (TR-pc-020).
178	- `restore(data: Dictionary, stored_version: int, ctx)` is **two-phase: decode and validate into scratch, then copy the contents into the existing block object**. This is the single wording of the rule; "whole-block replace" and "swaps whole tables from scratch" in owner GDDs mean *replace the block's contents*, never the object (registry `block_as_resource_or_node`; ADR-0003 § 2: read-view facades are long-lived).
179	- **Failure is reported through `ctx.fault(<OWNER>_RESTORE_*)`** with the owner's domain code and a named detail, never by return value and never by clamping; the kernel fires `load_failed` and Save/Load maps it to the `RESTORE_FAILED` class of SL-11. Owner GDDs that describe `(ok, reason, detail)` mean this (ADR-0003 sync, not this ADR's to change).
180	- `post_restore(ctx)` rebuilds derived caches and cross-block verification; `default_state(ctx)` fills a block missing from an older file whose `added_in_format` exceeds the file's `format_version`.
181	- A restore is idempotent: `snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` is canonical-byte identical except for the closed `REBASE_BLOCKS` list (SL-12), and the Graph's, Body's and Controller's tests prove it.
182	
183	**2.3 Block versions are data, cross-checked at boot.** `added_in_format`, `RETIRED_BLOCKS` and the mandatory flag live in one committed file `assets/data/saveload/block_versions.json` (loaded by ADR-0007's pipeline in the composition root as a closed-schema table and injected, with the Save/Load `ScalarTable`, into `SaveService.setup()` as plain data, so `save` needs no import edge to `data`; `save` may type variables with ADR-0007's published value types, TD-27), not in `BlockDescriptor`, so ADR-0003's descriptor field list is unchanged. After the registry freeze, the composition root runs `SaveBootCheck.verify(block_versions, registry_view)`: a mandatory-derivation mismatch, a registered block that is also retired (`SL_BOOT_RETIRED_BUT_REGISTERED`), or a missing entry fails boot with a domain-1 `SL_BOOT_*` code and the root never starts the kernel. A persisted WORLD block is **mandatory iff its `added_in_format` is at most the file's `format_version`**; the MVP set in SL-25 is the *result* of that rule, not a hand-kept list.
184	
185	**2.4 `registry_epoch` and `catalogue_version`.** `registry_epoch` (the header field that tells "the registry moved" from corruption) is the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 over the UTF-8 text of the sorted lines `block_id:schema_version:added_in_format\n` for every persisted block, as lowercase hex. It uses `HashingContext` directly, **not** H64 or the canonical encoding, so it depends on neither ADR-0005 nor the kernel. A file whose `registry_epoch` differs from the running build's and fails a mandatory-set or schema step is INCOMPATIBLE-dev: never CORRUPT, never quarantined (SL-11, T-5 steps 18 and 21). `catalogue_version` is the Item DB's single integer offered by ADR-0007 § 3.4; it is written in the header as an `int`, and its only gating use is the newer-than-build refusal of § 1.10.
186	
187	**2.5 `hash_algo` and `codec`.** `hash_algo` 2 names H64 (the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 via `HashingContext`, read little-endian, ratified by the GDD, owned by ADR-0005); 0 and 1 are reserved, never written (they are `hash_algo` ids, not hash values: no `H64` value is reserved as a sentinel, ADR-0005). An unsupported `hash_algo` skips the reproduction compare (`SL_VERIFY_ALGO_SKIPPED`, REBASED cause 4) so a kernel hash change is never a save-breaking event. `codec` 0 only.
188	
189	**2.6 Policy and fixtures (SL-14, unchanged).** The migration machinery exists from format 1. Two goldens: `tests/fixtures/saves/v1-standin/` (regenerated freely until the registry settles) and `tests/fixtures/saves/v1/` (generated from the real registry at the first outside build, immutable, with a CI schema-drift fingerprint: the `registry_epoch` of the committed shapes may change only together with a `schema_version` or `format_version` bump). The obligation to migrate begins with the first build given to anyone outside the project; before it, a mismatched development save is refused as "made by an incompatible development build". This is the same moment ADR-0007's id ledgers flip to `SHIPPED`; one project-level decision flips both.
